sections.html:
Pasco is the Franklin County seat and one of the Tri-Cities, with Kennewick and Richland across the Columbia River to the south. Pasco counted an estimated 82,848 residents on July 1, 2025, a rise of 7.1% over April 2020. The city covers about 34 square miles, roughly 30.5 of them land.

A seller here deals with city hall for permits and rental licenses, the Franklin County Treasurer for tax and excise payments, and the Pasco School District for school boundaries that buyers ask about.

Seven in ten homes have their owners living in them. Parts of Pasco are newer subdivisions and parts are older neighborhoods near downtown, so a nearby sale of a similar house is a better guide than the citywide median. Ask an agent or your cash buyer which recent sales they used. Buyers who commute across the river to Kennewick or Richland will weigh that trip against price.

sections.h2: Heat, cold and the items buyers check
sections.html:
Pasco sits in the rain shadow of the Cascade Range, so it is dry and windy. Summers run hot, and winters can get cold enough to freeze pipes. A few items get extra attention from buyers:

  • Air conditioning age and capacity, since cooling runs for months.
  • Roof condition and attic insulation under strong summer sun.
  • Irrigation systems and landscaping that live on little rain.
  • Pipes and exterior faucets that can freeze in a cold snap.

Keep service records for the cooling system and roof where a buyer can see them. A unit close to the end of its life belongs on the disclosure form, not in an inspector's surprise.

The Pasco School District runs the city's public schools. Pasco High School and Chiawana High School are the longer-standing high schools, and Sageview High School opened in 2025 to relieve crowding at Chiawana. Delta High School, a STEM program shared with the Kennewick and Richland districts, opened in 2015. Confirm the boundary for your address with the district before you quote a school in an ad, and tell buyers which of these campuses is closest.

Pasco's Ordinance No. 4770, adopted June 2, 2025, removed permit requirements for several small jobs, listed on the city's permit page. They matter if you want to tidy the house before listing:

  • One-story detached sheds or playhouses up to 200 square feet in residential areas.
  • Fences under 7 feet, retaining walls under 4 feet, and decks under 200 square feet and 30 inches high.
  • Residential roofing and siding replacement limited to shingles, underlayment, flashing, siding, barrier and veneer.

Structural work, anything habitable, and building in an easement or too close to a property line still need a permit. A permit is good for 180 days from issue, and passing an inspection renews that clock.

The city's ADU guide, published in 2023, allows one attached or detached ADU per residential parcel, up to 1,000 square feet or 55 percent of the main house, whichever is less. The unit must be long-term housing, with occupants living there more than 180 days a year, and short-term rentals are not allowed. Landlords need a rental business license under PMC 5.60.010. Call Pasco Community and Economic Development at (509) 545-3441 to confirm current rules for your zone.

sections.h2: Excise tax on a Pasco sale
sections.html:
This one is the seller's bill under RCW 82.45.080. State tax starts at 1.1% and tops out at 3% on the highest slice, and a local portion is added. The first band stops at $525,000 now, and from January 1, 2027 it stops at $551,000, with the later breakpoints rising to $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. The median value in Pasco falls in the first band. Franklin County's Treasurer will quote the local rate.

Your one-month grace period before interest begins at the notarization date of the deed. Affidavit, deed and payment all go to the county treasurer. Overpaid? File for a refund within four years of the sale; it goes to whoever paid. The Department of Revenue REET page has the forms.

sections.h2: Franklin County property taxes at closing
sections.html:
Taxes are payable on or after February 15, with the full amount due by April 30. Bills over $50 may be split, half by April 30 and half by October 31. The Treasurer is at 1016 N 4th Avenue in Pasco, phone 509-545-3518.

For real property, the Treasurer starts foreclosure action when taxes have been delinquent for three years, so a seller with old arrears should pay them off at closing. Ask your closing officer for a current tax status before you sign.

A deduction may be available to owners who are 61 or older or disabled, and to certain disabled service members. Applications go to the Franklin County Assessor, 509-545-3506. If you are selling because you can no longer keep up with the house, ask whether a reduction would have applied in a prior year. Taking five minutes to call the Assessor before closing can show a break you missed, and it costs nothing to ask.

An improved residential property needs a seller disclosure statement, handed over five business days after mutual acceptance unless the buyer waives it or the sale is exempt. List cooling, roof and irrigation history, which dry-climate buyers ask about most.

Pasco owners pick among an agent listing, a sale without an agent and an as-is cash deal. The deed, affidavit and tax steps do not change, so timing, condition and price decide.

  • Listing works when the house is in good shape and you can sit through showings and a buyer's financing.
  • Selling as-is for cash works better for deferred repairs, a tenant in place or an inherited property.
  • Whoever the buyer is, ask who pays the excise tax, how the sale date is set and how back taxes are dealt with.

If you inherited the house, check the tax status first. Old arrears are easier to clear from proceeds at closing than after, and the Treasurer can tell you where the account stands. A tenant in place calls for a lease copy and a plan for notice, so raise both with any buyer early. Whatever route you choose, line up the permit history, since sheds, fences and roofing changes are the items most likely to come up.

faqs.q: What excise tax applies to a Pasco house sale?
faqs.a: State tax begins at 1.1% on the first $525,000 under current rules and rises above that, with a Pasco local portion on top. Ask the Franklin County Treasurer for the local rate.

faqs.q: What are the Franklin County tax due dates?
faqs.a: Payment opens February 15. The whole bill is due April 30, or if it is over $50 you may pay half then and half by October 31.

faqs.q: Can I rent out an ADU in Pasco as a vacation rental?
faqs.a: No. The city's ADU guide requires long-term residential use, with occupants living there more than 180 days a year, and short-term rentals are not allowed.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for a new roof in Pasco?
faqs.a: Not for a shingle, underlayment and flashing replacement. Ordinance 4770 removed that requirement, but structural roof work still needs a permit.

faqs.q: Who handles tax breaks for senior or disabled owners in Franklin County?
faqs.a: The Franklin County Assessor at 509-545-3506. The county offers a deduction for owners who are 61 or older or disabled, and for certain disabled service members.
